knowledge_base.title: Python History
knowledge_base.content: Python was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. It emphasizes code readability and supports multiple programming paradigms including procedural, object-oriented, and functional programming.

knowledge_base.title: Solar System
knowledge_base.content: The Solar System has eight planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Jupiter is the largest planet, with a mass more than twice that of all other planets combined.

knowledge_base.title: Photosynthesis
knowledge_base.content: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants convert sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen. It takes place primarily in the leaves, within organelles called chloroplasts.

knowledge_base.title: HTTP Protocol
knowledge_base.content: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is the foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web. The most common HTTP methods are GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE. HTTPS adds encryption via TLS/SSL.

knowledge_base.title: Machine Learning Basics
knowledge_base.content: Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence where models learn from data. The three main types are supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning. Common algorithms include decision trees, neural networks, and support vector machines.

knowledge_base.title: DNA Structure
knowledge_base.content: DNA is a double helix composed of nucleotides containing four bases: adenine (A), thymine (T), guanine (G), and cytosine (C). Adenine pairs with thymine, and guanine pairs with cytosine. The human genome contains approximately 3 billion base pairs.

knowledge_base.title: Git Version Control
knowledge_base.content: Git is a distributed version control system created by Linus Torvalds in 2005. Key commands include git init, git add, git commit, git push, and git pull. Branches allow parallel development, and merging combines work from different branches.

knowledge_base.title: Water Cycle
knowledge_base.content: The water cycle describes the continuous movement of water on Earth. It includes evaporation from oceans and lakes, condensation forming clouds, precipitation as rain or snow, and collection in bodies of water. Transpiration from plants also contributes.

knowledge_base.title: REST API Design
knowledge_base.content: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style for designing web APIs. Key principles include statelessness, uniform interface, resource-based URLs, and using standard HTTP methods. Responses typically use JSON format.

knowledge_base.title: Roman Empire
knowledge_base.content: The Roman Empire was founded in 27 BC when Augustus became the first emperor. At its peak under Trajan (117 AD), it controlled the Mediterranean region, Western Europe, and parts of the Middle East. The Western Roman Empire fell in 476 AD.
